Six years ago today, we lost Congressman John Lewis. I walked the Edmund Pettus Bridge with him — the bridge where he was violently attacked for standing up for voting rights. 

His message has never been more important: the right to vote is precious. It’s sacred. It’s our job to carry on his torch.
posts.summary: Honors John Lewis's voting rights legacy, emphasizes voting rights protection

posts.text:
Every American has the right to vote. 

But the President continues to attack that right, including once again voting by mail (which he has done himself). 

He's relitigating an election he lost six years ago instead of focusing on what he should be fixing: costs are up for families across the country and his war has no end in sight. Despite everything he said tonight, Americans will go to the polls this fall because they don’t want more rubber stamps of Donald Trump.
posts.summary: Defends voting rights, criticizes Trump's election rhetoric

posts.text:
Minnesotans shouldn't have to wait longer for their mail simply because of where they live.

That's why I'm calling on the USPS to reverse changes that would slow mail delivery across Minnesota.

Reliable mail service matters for families, seniors, veterans, and small businesses. I'll keep fighting to make sure every Minnesota community gets the service it deserves.
